question: Under the Navigation Rules' definitions, what is a "masthead light"?
choice_a: A red light shown at the top of the mast, visible all around the horizon
choice_b: A white light placed over the vessel's fore-and-aft centerline, showing an unbroken light over 225 degrees, from dead ahead to 22.5 degrees abaft the beam on each side
choice_c: A flashing yellow light used only by anchored vessels
choice_d: A green light shown on the starboard side only, visible 112.5 degrees
explanation: A masthead light is a white light placed over the fore-and-aft centerline showing an unbroken light over an arc of 225 degrees, from dead ahead to 22.5 degrees abaft the beam on either side.

question: Per the Navigation Rules' definitions, what is a sidelight's arc of visibility?
choice_b: 225 degrees, matching the masthead light
choice_c: 112.5 degrees on its respective side, from dead ahead to 22.5 degrees abaft the beam
choice_d: 67.5 degrees, matching the sternlight
explanation: Sidelights (green to starboard, red to port) each show an unbroken arc of 112.5 degrees on their respective side, from dead ahead to 22.5 degrees abaft the beam.

question: What arc of visibility must a sternlight show, per the Navigation Rules' definitions?
choice_b: 360 degrees, all around the horizon
choice_c: 112.5 degrees, matching a sidelight
choice_d: 135 degrees, extending 67.5 degrees from right aft on each side
explanation: A sternlight shows an unbroken light over an arc of 135 degrees, extending 67.5 degrees from right aft on each side of the vessel.

question: A vessel under 20 meters in length may combine its red and green sidelights how?
choice_a: In one bi-color lantern carried on the vessel's fore-and-aft centerline
choice_b: They may not be combined under any circumstance
choice_c: By replacing them with a single all-round white light
choice_d: By mounting them on the port and starboard rails 20 meters apart
explanation: On a vessel of less than 20 meters, the sidelights may be combined in one lantern carried on the fore-and-aft centerline of the vessel.

question: What color is a "towing light," per the Navigation Rules' definitions, and what light does it match in characteristics?
choice_a: White, with the same characteristics as a masthead light
choice_b: Yellow, with the same characteristics as a sternlight
choice_c: Red, with the same characteristics as a sidelight
choice_d: Green, with the same characteristics as a sidelight
explanation: A towing light is a yellow light having the same characteristics as the sternlight.

question: Per the Navigation Rules' definitions, a "flashing light" flashes at what minimum frequency?
choice_b: 50 to 70 flashes per minute
choice_c: 120 or more flashes per minute
choice_d: Exactly 1 flash every 2 seconds
explanation: A "flashing light" is one which flashes at regular intervals at a frequency of 120 flashes or more per minute.

question: A power-driven vessel 12 meters or more but less than 50 meters in length must show a masthead light visible for how many miles (3 miles if the vessel is less than 20 meters)?
choice_b: 6 miles
choice_c: 1 mile
choice_d: 5 miles
explanation: Vessels 12 meters or more but less than 50 meters must show a masthead light visible for 5 miles, or 3 miles if the vessel is less than 20 meters in length.

question: A vessel 50 meters or more in length must show a masthead light visible for at least how many miles?
choice_b: 3 miles
choice_c: 2 miles
choice_d: 5 miles
explanation: Vessels 50 meters or more in length must show a masthead light visible for a minimum of 6 miles.

question: A power-driven vessel less than 12 meters in length may show which simplified lighting configuration instead of the standard masthead-plus-sidelights-plus-sternlight arrangement?
choice_a: A single red light visible all around the horizon
choice_b: An all-round white light and sidelights
choice_c: Sidelights only, with no white light
choice_d: A masthead light only, with no sidelights or sternlight
explanation: A power-driven vessel less than 12 meters in length may exhibit an all-round white light and sidelights instead of the standard masthead light, sidelights, and sternlight arrangement.

question: A power-driven vessel underway 50 meters or more in length must show which forward lighting arrangement, in addition to sidelights and a sternlight?
choice_b: An all-round white light in place of masthead lights
choice_c: Two masthead lights in a vertical line, the after one higher than the forward one
choice_d: Two masthead lights side by side at the same height
explanation: A power-driven vessel 50 meters or more in length must show two masthead lights in a vertical line, with the after light higher than the forward one, plus sidelights and a sternlight.

question: A vessel engaged in trawling must show which combination of all-round lights?
choice_a: Two all-round lights in a vertical line, the upper red and the lower white
choice_b: Three all-round red lights in a vertical line
choice_c: A single flashing yellow light
choice_d: Two all-round lights in a vertical line, the upper green and the lower white
explanation: A vessel engaged in trawling shall exhibit two all-round lights in a vertical line, the upper being green and the lower white.

question: A fishing vessel engaged in fishing OTHER than trawling must show which combination of all-round lights?
choice_a: Two all-round lights in a vertical line, the upper red and the lower white
choice_b: Two all-round lights in a vertical line, the upper green and the lower white
choice_c: A single all-round white light only
choice_d: Two all-round green lights in a vertical line
explanation: A vessel engaged in fishing other than trawling shall exhibit two all-round lights in a vertical line, the upper being red and the lower white.

question: A fishing vessel with outlying gear extending more than 150 meters horizontally must show what additional signal?
choice_b: An additional all-round white light in the direction of the gear
choice_c: A red flag by day and a red light by night
choice_d: Three short blasts every minute
explanation: When outlying fishing gear extends more than 150 meters horizontally from the vessel, an additional all-round white light shall be exhibited in the direction of the gear.

question: A vessel not under command must show which lights and shapes where they can best be seen?
choice_a: One all-round white light, and a single ball
choice_b: Red-white-red lights in a vertical line, and a ball-diamond-ball
choice_c: Two all-round red lights in a vertical line, and two balls in a vertical line
choice_d: A single flashing yellow light, no shapes required
explanation: A vessel not under command shall exhibit two all-round red lights in a vertical line, and two balls in a vertical line, where they can best be seen.

question: A vessel restricted in its ability to maneuver must show which vertical light and shape combination?
choice_a: Two all-round red lights, and two balls
choice_b: Green-white-green all-round lights, and three diamonds
choice_c: A single all-round red light, and a single diamond
choice_d: Red-white-red all-round lights in a vertical line, and a ball-diamond-ball shape combination
explanation: A vessel restricted in its ability to maneuver shall exhibit three all-round lights in a vertical line -- the highest and lowest red, the middle white -- and, by day, a ball-diamond-ball shape combination.

question: A vessel engaged in diving operations, when too small to exhibit the full restricted-in-ability-to-maneuver signals, may instead show what?
choice_a: A rigid replica of the International Code flag "A" (Alpha), not less than 1 meter in height
choice_b: A single red light visible all around
choice_c: Nothing -- diving vessels under a certain size are exempt from all signals
choice_d: A yellow flag with a black diagonal stripe
explanation: A vessel engaged in diving operations, when of a size that makes it impracticable to exhibit the full signals, may instead exhibit a rigid replica of the International Code flag "A" not less than 1 meter in height.

question: A vessel at anchor less than 50 meters in length may show which anchor light configuration, instead of separate forward and aft lights?
choice_a: Two all-round white lights, one forward and one aft, regardless of length
choice_b: A single all-round white light where it can best be seen
choice_c: A red light forward and a white light aft
choice_d: No anchor light is required for vessels under 50 meters
explanation: A vessel of less than 50 meters in length at anchor may exhibit a single all-round white light where it can best be seen, instead of the forward-and-aft two-light configuration required of larger vessels.

question: In addition to its anchor light, a vessel aground must show what additional lights and shapes, where practicable?
choice_a: A single flashing yellow light only
choice_b: Two green lights and a diamond
choice_c: Two all-round red lights in a vertical line, and three balls in a vertical line
choice_d: No additional signal is required beyond the anchor light
explanation: A vessel aground shall exhibit its anchor lights, plus two all-round red lights in a vertical line and three balls in a vertical line, where practicable.

question: A vessel less than 12 meters in length that runs aground is exempt from which requirement?
choice_a: Exhibiting any anchor light at all
choice_b: Sounding any sound signal in restricted visibility
choice_c: All navigation light requirements while aground
choice_d: Exhibiting the two red lights and three balls otherwise required for a vessel aground
explanation: A vessel of less than 12 meters in length when aground is not required to exhibit the two all-round red lights and three balls otherwise required of a grounded vessel.

question: In addition to sidelights and a sternlight, a sailing vessel underway may exhibit what optional signal at or near the top of the mast?
choice_a: Two all-round lights in a vertical line, the upper red and the lower green
choice_b: A single all-round white light
choice_c: Two all-round lights in a vertical line, the upper green and the lower red
choice_d: A flashing yellow light
explanation: A sailing vessel underway may, in addition to sidelights and a sternlight, exhibit two all-round lights in a vertical line at or near the top of the mast, the upper being red and the lower green -- but not together with the combined lantern option.

question: A sailing vessel proceeding under sail AND being propelled by machinery must exhibit which day shape forward?
choice_b: A conical shape, apex downward
choice_c: A diamond
choice_d: No day shape is ever required for a motor-sailing vessel
explanation: A vessel proceeding under sail and also being propelled by machinery shall exhibit forward, where best seen, a conical shape, apex downward, to indicate it is a power-driven vessel for right-of-way purposes.

question: How long is a "short blast," per the Navigation Rules' definitions?
choice_b: 4 to 6 seconds
choice_c: About 1 second
choice_d: About 10 seconds
explanation: A short blast is defined as a blast of about 1 second's duration.

question: How long is a "prolonged blast," per the Navigation Rules' definitions?
choice_b: 8 to 10 seconds
choice_c: 2 to 3 seconds
choice_d: 4 to 6 seconds
explanation: A prolonged blast is defined as a blast of from 4 to 6 seconds' duration.

question: Per the Navigation Rules, a vessel of what length or more must be provided with a whistle?
choice_b: 20 meters
choice_c: 50 meters
choice_d: 100 meters
explanation: A vessel of 12 meters or more in length must be provided with a whistle meeting the required specifications.

question: Per the Navigation Rules, a vessel of 20 meters or more in length must carry which sound signal appliance, in addition to a whistle?
choice_b: A bell
choice_c: An air horn only
choice_d: No additional appliance is required until 100 meters
explanation: A vessel of 20 meters or more in length must carry a bell in addition to a whistle.

question: A vessel 100 meters or more in length must carry which additional sound-signal appliance, beyond a whistle and bell?
choice_b: A siren
choice_c: A gong, with a tone that cannot be confused with the bell
choice_d: No additional appliance is required
explanation: A vessel 100 meters or more in length must carry a gong, the tone and sound of which cannot be confused with that of the bell, in addition to a whistle and bell.

question: What does three short blasts signal, per the Navigation Rules?
choice_a: I am overtaking you on your port side
choice_b: I am altering course to starboard
choice_c: I am at anchor
choice_d: I am operating astern propulsion
explanation: Three short blasts mean "I am operating astern propulsion."

question: A vessel intending to overtake another in a narrow channel and wanting to pass on the OTHER vessel's starboard side sounds what signal?
choice_b: Two short blasts
choice_c: One prolonged blast
choice_d: Five short blasts
explanation: A vessel intending to overtake another in a narrow channel signals one short blast to mean "I intend to overtake you on your starboard side."

question: In restricted visibility, a power-driven vessel making way through the water must sound what signal, at intervals of not more than 2 minutes?
choice_b: One prolonged blast
choice_c: One prolonged followed by two short blasts
choice_d: Rapid ringing of a bell for 5 seconds
explanation: In or near an area of restricted visibility, a power-driven vessel making way through the water sounds one prolonged blast at intervals of not more than 2 minutes.

question: In restricted visibility, a power-driven vessel underway but stopped and making no way through the water must sound what signal?
choice_b: One short blast repeated every minute
choice_c: Two prolonged blasts in succession, with about a 2-second interval between them
choice_d: Five short blasts
explanation: A power-driven vessel underway but stopped, making no way through the water, sounds two prolonged blasts in succession, with an interval of about 2 seconds between them.

question: In restricted visibility, a sailing vessel, a vessel not under command, or a vessel engaged in fishing must sound what signal at intervals of not more than 2 minutes?
choice_b: Two prolonged blasts
choice_c: Three short blasts
choice_d: One prolonged blast followed by two short blasts
explanation: A sailing vessel, a vessel not under command, or a vessel engaged in fishing sounds one prolonged blast followed by two short blasts at intervals of not more than 2 minutes in restricted visibility.

question: In restricted visibility, a vessel at anchor must ring a bell rapidly for about how long, at intervals of not more than 1 minute?
choice_b: About 1 second
choice_c: About 30 seconds
choice_d: About 10 seconds
explanation: A vessel at anchor in restricted visibility rings the bell rapidly for about 5 seconds at intervals of not more than 1 minute.

question: A vessel 100 meters or more in length at anchor in restricted visibility must, in addition to ringing the bell forward, do what?
choice_a: Fire a distress signal every 2 minutes
choice_b: Sound a gong for about 5 seconds in the after part of the vessel
choice_c: Sound one prolonged blast every minute
choice_d: Display a flashing red light
explanation: A vessel 100 meters or more in length at anchor must, in addition to the bell signal forward, sound a gong for about 5 seconds immediately after the bell, in the after part of the vessel.
